A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the critical current in the bilayer Nb/Ni can be enhanced by the surface barrier effect of a magnetic layer in a tilted field.
a magnetic layer with a small thickness can strongly affect the critical current of a superconductor in finite magnetic fields.
the magnetic field due to the magnetic layer can be a key factor for the critical current of a superconductor with the surface barrier effect.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the surface barrier effect can be used to enhance the critical current in a wide range magnetic fields and the effect is not limited to the magnetic field applied perpendicular to the plane.
the critical currents in superconductors can be enhanced in the presence of magnetic layers by taking advantage of the surface barrier effect.
we can use magnetic layers to control the vortex motion in superconductors.
